findings.claim: The strict-catalogue seam changes the exception class raised inside run.run()'s own try block without declaring any task-side surfacing duty. The contract says duplicate members raise `envelope.OutputsError` and then specifies only the dispatch mapping ('Dispatch retains exact source bytes/digest and maps that exception to its existing C2 refusal'). run.py:1210-1242 calls load_jobs() inside `try:` whose handler is `except (RunError, TypeError)`; OutputsError subclasses EnvelopeError(ValueError) and is not caught, so a duplicate member in the default catalogue escapes run() and main() (run.py:1289-1326 has no handler) as a traceback instead of the invalid envelope + exit 2 the task wire and the retained MainIsACli/call_run assertions require. §Statuses (task/CONTRACT.md:145-162) does not cover library exceptions either. One sentence naming the task-side mapping (invalid envelope, note, exit 2) closes it.
